properties.title: Tornado Warning issued November 26 at 11:58AM PST until November 26 at 12:15PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
TORSEW

The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Central King County in west central Washington...

* Until 1215 PM PST.

* At 1140 AM PST, a landspout was located near Renton, moving east
at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Weather spotters confirmed landspout.

IMPACT...Possible damage to mobile homes, roofs, and vehicles.

* The tornado will be near...
Snoqualmie around 1205 PM PST.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Fall
City, Mirrormont, Tanner, and Hobart.
properties.instruction:
To repeat, a tornado is on the ground. TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a
basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy
building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors or in a vehicle, move to
the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying
debris.

To report severe weather contact your nearest law enforcement agency.
They will send your report to the National Weather Service office in
Seattle.

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:45AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
At 1145 AM PST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Issaquah, or 8 miles southeast of Bellevue, moving northeast at 40
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Bellevue, North Bend, Carnation, Redmond, Sammamish, Issaquah,
Snoqualmie, Fall City, Lake Marcel-Stillwater, Mirrormont, Pine
Lake, Union Hill-Novelty Hill, Sahalee, Hobart, Tanner, West Lake
Sammamish, Maple Heights-Lake Desire and Eastgate.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 918 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26, +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, +1.7
ft MHHW (6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.2 ft MHHW
(6.1 ft MLLW) at 4:53 PM Sun 11/29.
* West Sacramento: +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26, +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, +1.8
ft MHHW (6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.4 ft MHHW
(5.8 ft MLLW) at 8:03 PM Sun 11/29.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27, +7.3 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28,
+6.7 ft at 9:00 AM Sun 11/29, and +6.3 ft at 9:00 AM Mon
11/30.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 8:45AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends will remain
generally steady between 18.0 feet to 18.3 feet into the weekend and
early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Thursday was 18.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 18.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady with Major Flood
Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 4:34AM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
